items.title: kick-silhouette-break
items.claim: In Images 13 and 19, the white fighter’s raised trouser leg ends without a visibly distinguishable foot, unlike the clearly visible raised foot in Image 22.
items.reason: The striking limb is the focal point of a fighter; an unreadable endpoint makes the pose look unfinished and obscures its reach.
items.suggest: Review these poses at phone size and adjust the artwork or silhouette so the foot is distinguishable from the trouser cuff; animation playback would establish whether this is only a transitional pose.

items.title: instructions-detached-from-sticks
items.claim: In Image 3, the movement and attack meanings appear in a separate text strip above the sticks, while the sticks themselves display only directional marks.
items.reason: A new player must translate between the legend and two thumb surfaces instead of recognizing actions where they touch.
items.suggest: Place concise action labels around each stick during onboarding, with stance and technique distinguished consistently, rather than concentrating both mappings in a separate strip.

items.title: intro-copy-competes-with-matchup
items.claim: In Image 2, the opponent description and control explanation share one prominent dark panel between the matchup heading and the fighters.
items.reason: The introduction mixes opponent personality with operating instructions, weakening the immediate visual hierarchy of who to fight and how to begin.
items.suggest: Keep one short opponent cue on the round card and move the control explanation into a distinct, visually demonstrated first-fight instruction.

items.title: settings-panel-cuts-through-fighters
items.claim: In Image 7, the settings panel ends across the fighters’ bodies, leaving their lower legs and the arena exposed beneath its straight bottom edge.
items.reason: The exposed body fragments make the settings screen feel like an abruptly cropped overlay rather than a deliberately composed mobile screen.
items.suggest: Extend the settings backdrop to the bottom of the viewport, or use a clearly bounded sheet with a uniformly dimmed game beneath it.

items.title: desktop-control-strip-dead-space
items.claim: In Image 9, the bottom control area contains a stick at each outer edge and a broad empty center, while the fight occupies the band above it.
items.reason: The empty strip draws attention to the interface footprint without adding useful information or spectacle.
items.suggest: On desktop, overlay compact secondary controls on the arena or reduce the dedicated control strip, giving the fight more of the available screen while preserving readable keyboard hints.
